result.markdown: --- title: "Notebooks as Posts: An R Demo" subtitle: "Same pipeline, different kernel: this one runs through R's knitr engine" date: 2026-07-25 status: "seedling" categories: ["meta"] tags: ["meta", "quarto", "r"] tableStyle: "striped" --- Quarto doesn't care which language produced the numbers — the same `.qmd` → Hugo pipeline used in the {{< post slug="quarto-python-demo" text="Python demo" >}} works for R too, executed through knitr instead of Jupyter. {{< cite quarto2026 >}} {{< cite xie2015 >}} A simple random walk, simulated and summarized: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(42) steps <- sample(c(-1, 1), 500, replace = TRUE) walk <- cumsum(steps) summary(walk) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Min. 1st Qu. Median Mean 3rd Qu. Max. -6.00 11.00 13.00 13.18 16.00 28.00 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot(walk, type = "l", col = "#a8071a", lwd = 1.5, axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "", panel.first = abline(h = 0, col = "#888", lty = 2)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index.markdown_strict_files/figure-markdown_strict/unnamed-chunk-2-1.png){width=768} ::: ::: Data frames render as ordinary tables, the same way they would in any other Quarto document: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} knitr::kable(head(data.frame(step = seq_along(walk), position = walk), 5)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} | step| position| |----:|--------:| | 1| -1| | 2| -2| | 3| -3| | 4| -4| | 5| -3| ::: ::: The point, same as the Python post: this table and plot are computed by R at build time, not maintained by hand. {{< references >}}
